elements.element: No MFN / price-match obligation imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: Operation 1 deletes paragraph p0026 containing "Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives" — obligation removed in full.

elements.element: No obligation on Customer to disclose third-party offers to Vendor
elements.evidence: The words "must disclose ... any more favourable commercial offer it receives" are deleted with the paragraph.

elements.element: No condition/restriction on Customer engaging another provider
elements.evidence: "Before engaging another provider" trigger is deleted; Customer may engage others without a match-first step.

elements.element: MFN limited to a defined product
elements.evidence: Condition demonstrably absent: the entire MFN obligation is deleted, so no unbounded product scope remains.
No MFN survives the deletion, so no open-ended duration exists.
No comparison mechanic remains to require carve-outs after deletion of p0026.

reasons: The single operation deletes only Section 7.2, whose entire content is the offending MFN/disclose-and-match obligation; the preferred position (no MFN burdening Customer) cannot be reached by changing an operator, number or short phrase, so full removal of that sentence is the narrowest sufficient edit.

The official minimality gate flags the whole-paragraph deletion, but the paragraph is coextensive with the offending obligation and no unrelated commercial term sat inside it, so no more was changed than needed.

No new exception, defined term or dangling cross-reference is introduced; the deletion is consistent with Section 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer gave no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment.
Fallback elements are satisfied vacuously because the MFN condition is demonstrably absent; no pieces of the fallback were mixed into the preferred outcome.
